claims.text: Bilateral hilar adenopathy is the most common abnormality; sarcoidosis is most often suspected when hilar adenopathy, with or without lung infiltrates, is found incidentally on a chest radiograph
claims.quote: Sarcoidosis is most often suspected when hilar adenopathy, with or without lung infiltrates, is incidentally detected on chest radiography. Bilateral hilar adenopathy is the most common abnormality.

claims.text: CXR stages (spontaneous remission): 0 normal chest radiograph; I bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy without pulmonary infiltrates (60–80%); II bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with pulmonary infiltrates (50–65%); III pulmonary infiltrates without bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (< 30%); IV pulmonary fibrosis (0%)
claims.quote: 0 | Normal chest radiograph | — | I | Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy without pulmonary infiltrates | 60–80% | II | Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with pulmonary infiltrates | 50–65% | III | Pulmonary infiltrates without bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy | < 30% | IV | Pulmonary fibrosis | 0%

claims.text: A normal chest radiograph (stage 0) does not exclude sarcoidosis, particularly when cardiac or neurologic involvement is suspected; high-resolution CT is more sensitive for hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy and parenchymal abnormalities
claims.quote: A normal chest radiograph (stage 0) does not exclude the diagnosis of sarcoidosis, particularly when cardiac or neurologic involvement is suspected. A high-resolution CT is more sensitive for detecting hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy and parenchymal abnormalities.

claims.text: Lung parenchymal involvement is predominantly in the upper lobes but can be in any part of the lungs
claims.quote: Lung parenchymal involvement is predominantly in the upper lobes but can be in any part of lungs.

claims.text: Staging by chest radiograph can mislead about severity: cardiac or neurologic sarcoidosis can portend a poor prognosis without evidence of lung involvement
claims.quote: However, staging sarcoidosis by chest radiography can be misleading in regard to predicting disease severity; for example, extrapulmonary sarcoidosis, such as cardiac sarcoidosis or neurologic sarcoidosis, can portend a poor prognosis in the absence of evidence of pulmonary involvement.

claims.text: Causes An inflammatory disorder with noncaseating granulomas in one or more organs and tissues; etiology is unknown; the lungs and lymphatic system are most often affected, but any organ can be
claims.quote: Sarcoidosis is an inflammatory disorder resulting in noncaseating granulomas in one or more organs and tissues; etiology is unknown. The lungs and lymphatic system are most often affected, but sarcoidosis may affect any organ.

claims.text: Systemic and extrapulmonary involvement is common, but > 90% of adult patients have pulmonary involvement
claims.quote: Systemic and extrapulmonary involvement is common with sarcoidosis, but > 90% of adult patients have pulmonary involvement.

claims.text: Symptoms Pulmonary symptoms range from none to cough, exertional dyspnea and, rarely, lung or other organ failure
claims.quote: Pulmonary symptoms range from none to cough, exertional dyspnea and, rarely, lung or other organ failure.

claims.text: Löfgren syndrome: a triad of acute migratory polyarthritis, erythema nodosum and hilar adenopathy; fever, malaise, uveitis and parotitis may also be present; self-limited, and usually treated with NSAIDs alone
claims.quote: Löfgren syndrome manifests as a triad of acute migratory polyarthritis, erythema nodosum, and hilar adenopathy (3). Fever, malaise, uveitis, and parotitis may also be present. Löfgren syndrome is more common among people of European ancestry. Löfgren syndrome is self-limited. Patients can usually be treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) alone.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: ACE level; biopsy: non-caseating granulomas; steroids if symptomatic
claims.quote: ACE level, biopsy non-caseating granulomas; steroids if symptomatic

claims.text: Get chest imaging, but confirm by biopsy, usually endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration of a mediastinal or hilar lymph node
claims.quote: Obtain a chest imaging study but confirm the diagnosis by biopsy, usually endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration of a mediastinal or hilar lymph node.

claims.text: Systemic corticosteroids when indicated (eg, severe symptoms, hypercalcemia, progressive decline in organ function, cardiac or neurologic involvement)
claims.quote: Treat patients with systemic corticosteroids when indicated (eg, severe symptoms, hypercalcemia, progressive decline in organ function, cardiac or neurologic involvement).

claims.text: Other immunosuppressants if moderate corticosteroid doses are not tolerated, the disease is corticosteroid-resistant, or corticosteroids would be needed long term
claims.quote: Treat with other immunosuppressants if patients cannot tolerate moderate doses of corticosteroids, sarcoidosis is resistant to corticosteroids, or if corticosteroids are required long term.
